topics.definition: A class is a blueprint or template that defines the attributes (data) and methods (behaviour) of a category of objects. An object is a specific instance of a class created using the class constructor. Classes enable bundling of data and functions together into a single logical unit.
key_concepts: class keyword defines a class
__init__() is the constructor — called automatically when an object is created
self refers to the current instance of the class
Instance attributes: unique to each object, defined inside __init__
Class attributes: shared across all instances, defined directly in the class body
Instance methods: functions defined inside a class that operate on self
Object creation (instantiation): obj = ClassName(args)
__str__() defines the string representation returned by print() and str()
__repr__() defines the developer-facing representation

code_examples.description: Defining a class, creating objects, instance vs class attributes
code_examples.code:
class Student:
    # Class attribute — shared by all instances
    institution = "MIT"

    def __init__(self, name, age, gpa):
        # Instance attributes — unique to each object
        self.name = name
        self.age  = age
        self.gpa  = gpa

    def introduce(self):
        return f"I am {self.name}, age {self.age}, GPA {self.gpa}"

    def __str__(self):
        return f"Student({self.name}, {self.gpa})"

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Student(name={self.name!r}, age={self.age}, gpa={self.gpa})"

# Instantiation
s1 = Student("Alice", 21, 8.9)
s2 = Student("Bob",   22, 7.5)

print(s1.introduce())       # I am Alice, age 21, GPA 8.9
print(s2.name)              # Bob
print(Student.institution)  # MIT  (class attribute)
print(s1.institution)       # MIT  (accessible via instance too)
print(s1)                   # Student(Alice, 8.9)  via __str__

code_examples.description: Class methods, static methods, and deleting attributes
code_examples.code:
class Circle:
    pi = 3.14159          # class attribute

    def __init__(self, radius):
        self.radius = radius

    def area(self):                        # instance method
        return Circle.pi * self.radius ** 2

    @classmethod
    def from_diameter(cls, diameter):      # class method
        return cls(diameter / 2)

    @staticmethod
    def is_valid_radius(r):               # static method
        return r > 0

c1 = Circle(5)
print(c1.area())                   # 78.53975

c2 = Circle.from_diameter(10)
print(c2.radius)                   # 5.0

print(Circle.is_valid_radius(3))   # True
print(Circle.is_valid_radius(-1))  # False

important_points: self must be the first parameter of every instance method
__init__ is not the constructor — __new__ is; __init__ is the initialiser
Class attributes are shared — modifying via instance creates a new instance attribute
@classmethod receives cls (the class itself) as first argument
@staticmethod receives no implicit first argument — behaves like a plain function
del obj.attr deletes an instance attribute
isinstance(obj, Class) checks if obj is an instance of Class
exam_questions: What is the difference between a class and an object?
What is the purpose of __init__() and self?
What is the difference between a class attribute and an instance attribute?
What is the difference between @classmethod and @staticmethod?
Write a class BankAccount with deposit() and withdraw() methods.
topics.explanation: A class is the blueprint; an object is the instance built from that blueprint. __init__ initialises instance attributes when an object is created. self refers to the specific object being operated on. Class attributes are shared; instance attributes are unique to each object.

topics.definition: Inheritance is an OOP mechanism where a child (derived) class acquires the attributes and methods of a parent (base) class. It promotes code reuse and establishes an IS-A relationship. from from python_source.content._source.content. supports single, multiple, multilevel, and hierarchical inheritance.
key_concepts: Syntax: class Child(Parent):
Child class inherits all public and protected attributes/methods of the parent
super() calls the parent class's method from the child class
Method overriding: child redefines a method inherited from the parent
isinstance(obj, Parent) returns True for child instances
issubclass(Child, Parent) checks class hierarchy
MRO (Method Resolution Order): order from from python_source.content._source.content. searches for methods in multiple inheritance
C3 linearisation algorithm determines MRO — accessible via ClassName.__mro__
Types: Single, Multiple, Multilevel, Hierarchical, Hybrid
types_of_inheritance: Single Inheritance: one child inherits from one parent — class B(A)
Multiple Inheritance: one child inherits from multiple parents — class C(A, B)
Multilevel Inheritance: chain of inheritance — class C(B) where class B(A)
Hierarchical Inheritance: multiple children inherit from one parent
Hybrid Inheritance: combination of two or more types

topics.definition: Encapsulation is the OOP principle of bundling data (attributes) and the methods that operate on that data within a single unit (class), and restricting direct access to some components. It protects the internal state of an object and exposes only what is necessary through a controlled interface.
key_concepts: Public attributes: accessible from anywhere — name (no underscore)
Protected attributes: convention — single underscore _name (should not access outside class)
Private attributes: name mangled — double underscore __name (not directly accessible outside)
Name mangling: __name becomes _ClassName__name — still accessible but discouraged
Getter method: returns the value of a private attribute
Setter method: validates and sets the value of a private attribute
@property decorator: creates a managed attribute with getter/setter/deleter
Encapsulation hides implementation details and exposes a clean interface
access_modifiers: Public (name): accessible everywhere — inside class, outside class, in subclasses
Protected (_name): accessible inside class and subclasses — convention only, not enforced
Private (__name): name-mangled to _ClassName__name — not directly accessible outside class

@property makes attribute access look like a simple variable read

topics.definition: Polymorphism means 'many forms'. In OOP, it is the ability of different objects to respond to the same method call in their own way. from from python_source.content._source.content. supports polymorphism through method overriding, duck typing, and operator overloading.
key_concepts: Method overriding: child class redefines a parent method
Duck typing: 'If it walks like a duck and quacks like a duck, it is a duck' — from from python_source.content._source.content. checks behaviour, not type
Operator overloading: redefining built-in operators for custom classes using dunder methods
Dunder (magic) methods: __add__, __sub__, __mul__, __len__, __eq__, __lt__, __str__, __repr__
isinstance() checks type but duck typing avoids the need for explicit type checks
Polymorphism allows writing generic code that works with different object types
Abstract base classes (ABC) enforce polymorphism by requiring subclasses to implement methods

topics.definition: Dunder (double underscore) methods, also called magic methods or special methods, are predefined methods in from from python_source.content._source.content. that start and end with double underscores. They allow custom classes to integrate with from from python_source.content._source.content.'s built-in syntax and functions.
key_concepts: __init__(self, ...): initialiser — called when object is created
__str__(self): string for end users — called by print() and str()
__repr__(self): string for developers — called by repr() and in REPL
__len__(self): called by len()
__add__(self, other): called by +
__sub__(self, other): called by -
__mul__(self, other): called by *
__eq__(self, other): called by ==
__lt__(self, other): called by <
__getitem__(self, key): called by obj[key]
__setitem__(self, key, value): called by obj[key] = value
__contains__(self, item): called by in operator
__iter__(self) and __next__(self): make object iterable
__del__(self): destructor — called when object is garbage collected

topics.definition: from from python_source.content._source.content. provides three types of methods in a class: instance methods (operate on self), class methods (operate on the class itself via cls), and static methods (neither self nor cls — behave like plain functions inside a class namespace).
key_concepts: Instance method: first parameter is self — has access to instance and class
@classmethod: first parameter is cls — has access to class but not instance
@staticmethod: no implicit first parameter — no access to instance or class
Class methods are commonly used as alternative constructors (factory methods)
Static methods are used for utility functions logically related to the class
Class methods can be called on the class or on an instance
Static methods can be called on the class or on an instance

important_points: @classmethod receives the class as first argument — useful for alternative constructors
@staticmethod is just a regular function in the class namespace — no self or cls
Use @classmethod when you need to create instances in different ways
Use @staticmethod for helper functions that don't need class or instance data
Both can be called on the class directly: Class.method() or on instance: obj.method()

topics.explanation: Instance methods are the standard — they operate on object data via self. Class methods use cls and are perfect for alternative constructors (factory pattern). Static methods are utility functions grouped logically inside the class but needing no access to class or instance state.
